feedback: The graph only compares the actual grade with a self-reported required grade; it never verifies that the required grade is the exact Table 8 selection for the supplied as-built thickness, Polar Class, material class, and strength category. Add a bounded Table 8 lookup constraint covering those selectors, require the selected required grade/rank to match that lookup, and then retain the correctly directed actual-rank >= required-rank comparison; missing selectors or unmatched table rows must fail. Also ensure each steel-grade requirement case is the same table-lookup case reached through hasTableLookupCase, rather than allowing an unrelated lookup case to satisfy that ship property. Finally, because the source is an every-plating rule and does not independently require RDF case existence, remove the top-level sh:minCount 1 requirements on hasSteelGradeRequirementCase and hasTableLookupCase while continuing to validate every case that is present.

Retain the correctly directed actual-rank >= required-rank comparison. Locate the absent canonical Table 8 row/grade values through the matcher rather than inventing them. Preserve optional top-level case existence. Remove the blanket sh:node constraint on every hasTableLookupCase value, because it incorrectly forces unrelated lookup cases to be steel-grade cases; instead validate each present hasSteelGradeRequirementCase and require that same node to be linked through hasTableLookupCase. Also encode all declared COMPLETE-contract terms currently omitted, including the ship-owned asBuiltThickness, materialClass, and steelGrade fields, without relocating their owners or silently substituting the case-owned specialized properties.
